source_text: Donec Moyses in Aegypto omni sapientia Aegyptiorum erudiretur, non erat gracili voce nec tardus lingua. Ubi vocem Dei audivit, sensit exilem vocem et impeditam linguam; se mutum profitetur coram Verbo quod in principio apud Deum erat. Homo mutis animalibus eloquens, eruditis mutus, apud divinam sapientiam iumentum — ut David: ut iumentum factus sum apud te. Omnes ad comparationem verbi divini muti sunt.
pass_a_gloss: While Moses in Egypt with-all wisdom of-Egyptians was-trained, not he-was with-thin voice nor slow of-tongue. When voice of-God he-heard, he-felt thin voice and hindered tongue; himself mute he-professes before Word which in beginning with God was. Man to-mute animals eloquent, to-learned mute, before divine wisdom beast — as David: as beast I-was-made before you. All to comparison of-word divine mute are.
pass_b_english: While Moses was still [[trained in all the wisdom of the Egyptians >> Bible:Acts 7:22]], he was neither [[slow of speech nor slow of tongue >> Bible:Exodus 4:10]]. Once he heard God’s voice, he felt his speech thin and his tongue hindered; before the [[Word that was in the beginning with God >> Bible:John 1:1]] he names himself mute. A rational man looks eloquent beside mute beasts, mute beside the learned, and — before divine Wisdom — a beast, as David said: [[I became as a beast before you >> Bible:Psalm 73:22]]. Beside the divine Word every human tongue is dumb.
